APPLICATION BOUNDARIES

Permission before action.

The model proposes. Application code decides what can execute.

Design decisions ↗
THE EXECUTION PATH
01Untrusted inputMessages, documents,
and tool observations
→
02Model proposalA structured request
to use a tool
→
03 / ENFORCEAuthorizationIdentity, action, resource,
role and approval
→
04Authorized resultReceipt-backed facts
for a supported answer

Detector alerts and audit events support evaluation. Authorization operates independently of whether suspicious content is detected.

01 / IDENTITY & RESOURCES

Keep identity outside the prompt.

Fixture bearer tokens identify Alice or Bob. A message claiming to be an administrator cannot replace that identity. Ownership and agent permissions are checked before operations.

Synthetic identity · production login not implemented
02 / RESPONSE INTEGRITY

Deliver supported facts.

The grounded response contract renders authorized receipts and maintained support policy. It constrains arbitrary model text, with tradeoffs for languages, formatting and open-ended tasks.

Inspect the output boundary ↗
03 / REQUEST CAPABILITIES

Make writes explicit and bounded.

The later hardening pass defaults to read-only request scope. Ticket creation needs separate consent, with at most one ticket and four tool attempts per scoped request.

Later control · separate deterministic evidence
04 / APPROVAL & STATE

Use approval once. Start fresh.

Fixture refund approvals expire and are consumed atomically. Agent runs receive fresh evidence and budgets. Replay prevention is process-local, rather than a distributed approval service.

Inspect boundary verification ↗
REPRODUCIBILITY & LIMITS

Evidence you can inspect.

Different checks answer different questions. Keep their populations separate.

THE CONTENT DETECTOR

Alerts have a cost.

Complete hardened sample

Attack intent labels were frozen separately from detector and authorization return values.

A missed alert and an executed unauthorized action are different outcomes. The gateway does not depend on this detector.
WHAT THIS STUDY DOES NOT ESTABLISH

Keep the limits visible.

  • One local model, one seed and small attack populations.
  • Project-authored labels and internal held-out variants.
  • Exact-marker checks can miss semantic leakage.
  • No full public benchmark or adaptive attack campaign.
  • Real authentication and distributed approvals remain future work.
NEXT EVALUATION ENVIRONMENT
